The mRNA-expression-based stemness index (mRNAsi) is the **first principal component** of a stemness gene-signature expression matrix, rescaled to 0–1 \[1\]. Publication figures sort samples by mRNAsi and stack the known clinical features underneath as colour strips, so the reader sees which subgroups carry the dedifferentiated end of the axis.

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming Language: R

-   Dependent packages: `ComplexHeatmap`; `ggplot2`; `dplyr`; `circlize`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
# Installing necessary packages
if (!requireNamespace("ComplexHeatmap", quietly = TRUE)) {
  BiocManager::install("ComplexHeatmap")
}
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("ggplot2")
}
if (!requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("dplyr")
}
if (!requireNamespace("circlize", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("circlize")
}

# Load packages
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(circlize)
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

With real data, mRNAsi comes from projecting your tumour expression matrix onto the PCBC stemness signature (the reference workflow's `pcbc-stemsig` file). We simulate the projection output directly: 60 medulloblastoma-like samples, a continuous mRNAsi, and two clinical features.

```{r load data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(1101)
n_sam <- 60
samples <- paste0("MB-", sprintf("%02d", 1:n_sam))
subgroup <- sample(c("Group3", "SHH", "Group4", "WNT"), n_sam,
                   replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1))
metastasis <- sample(c("M0", "M1"), n_sam, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.6, 0.4))
# latent stemness z-score: Group3/Group4 high, WNT low, M1 higher (as in the
# reference) — rescale to 0..1 only AFTER the effects, and do NOT re-sort, or
# the values decouple from the clinical features
z <- rnorm(n_sam) + 0.9 * (subgroup %in% c("Group3", "Group4")) -
  0.8 * (subgroup == "WNT") + 0.3 * (metastasis == "M1")
mRNAsi <- pnorm(z)

clin <- data.frame(sample = samples,
                   mRNAsi = mRNAsi,
                   Subgroup = subgroup,
                   Metastasis = metastasis)
head(clin, 3)
```

## Visualization

### 1. Samples Sorted by mRNAsi with Clinical Strips

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1mRNAsiHeatmap
#| fig-cap: "Samples sorted by mRNAsi (top gradient row) with subgroup and metastasis strips; the dedifferentiated end enriches for Group 3/4 and M1."
#| out.width: "95%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3

ord <- order(clin$mRNAsi)
mat <- rbind(mRNAsi = clin$mRNAsi[ord])
rownames(mat) <- "mRNAsi"
col_fun <- circlize::colorRamp2(c(0, 0.5, 1), c("#445EAD", "white", "#B31E22"))

ha_top <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  mRNAsi = anno_simple(mat["mRNAsi", ], col = col_fun),
  Subgroup = clin$Subgroup[ord],
  Metastasis = clin$Metastasis[ord],
  col = list(Subgroup = c("Group3" = "#B31E22", "SHH" = "#529B40",
                          "Group4" = "#383D8E", "WNT" = "#EABF00"),
             Metastasis = c(M0 = "#dcddde", M1 = "#700353")),
  annotation_name_side = "left")

Heatmap(mat, name = "mRNAsi", top_annotation = ha_top,
        col = col_fun, cluster_columns = FALSE, cluster_rows = FALSE,
        show_column_names = FALSE, show_row_names = FALSE,
        border = TRUE, width = unit(18, "cm"))
```

### 2. mRNAsi by Molecular Subgroup

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.2mRNAsiBox
#| fig-cap: "mRNAsi across medulloblastoma subgroups; the Kruskal-Wallis p value is annotated."
#| out.width: "65%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5

p_kw <- kruskal.test(mRNAsi ~ Subgroup, data = clin)$p.value
sub_order <- c("WNT", "SHH", "Group4", "Group3")

ggplot(clin, aes(factor(Subgroup, sub_order), mRNAsi, fill = Subgroup)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Group3" = "#B31E22", "SHH" = "#529B40",
                               "Group4" = "#383D8E", "WNT" = "#EABF00")) +
  labs(title = sprintf("mRNAsi by subgroup (Kruskal-Wallis %s)",
       ifelse(p_kw < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p_kw))),
       x = NULL, y = "mRNAsi", fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   mDNAsi (the methylation-based index) is drawn with the identical layout — swap the top row and re-run.
-   The strips must be ordered by the same sort as the index; annotating an unsorted matrix destroys the whole point of the figure.
-   For real data, project your log2-expression matrix onto the PCBC signature with `prcomp()` and take PC1 (`mRNAsi = PC1 / max(PC1)` rescaled to 0–1); the reference workflow ships the signature file.
:::

## Application

Stemness indices are compared across molecular subgroups, stages and therapies; high-mRNAsi tumours are typically the dedifferentiated, aggressive end of the cohort. The sorted-strip figure is the standard overview.

## Reference

\[1\] Malta TM, Sokolov A, Gentles AJ, et al. Machine learning identifies stemness features associated with oncogenic dedifferentiation. Cell. 2018;173(2):338-354.e15. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.034

\[2\] Xiaofan Lu, et al. FigureYa: A Standardized Visualization Framework for Enhancing Biomedical Data Interpretation and Research Efficiency. iMetaMed. 2025. doi:10.1002/imm3.70005
